To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crystal structures of the histone methyltransferases SET7/9 and SET9 in complexes with two inhibitors, DAAM-3 or AAM-1 that are amine derivatives of S-adenosyl-L-methionine, were determined, and the structural basis for the inhibitory action of the inhibitors is discussed.
the structures of SET7 and SET9 in complexes with AdoMet analogs reveal the molecular basis of their inhibition and provide insight into their substrate recognition.
the crystal structure of a histone lysine methyltransferases in complex with a novel AdoMet analogue, which is a weak inhibitor, reveals the structural basis of its inhibitory mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of inhibitors that mimic the methylated lysines of histone H3, which are the substrates of SET7/
the development of novel inhibitors of SET family methyltransferases and the design of inhibitors that target the substrate binding pocket of SET7/

the design of novel SET7/9 inhibitors, and the crystal structures of SET-9 in complexes with DAAM-3 or AAM-1 provide insights into how the alkyl chains of the inhibitors are accommodated in the substrate-binding site and lysine-access channel, and how they affect complex formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alkyl chain in the azaadenine analogue DAAM-3 binds in the lysyl-binding pocket and the alkyl chain with an n-hexane group in the AdoMet analogue AAM-1 binds in the lysinyl-access channel.
the alkyl chains of DAAM- and AAM-based inhibitors are not only involved in the stabilization of complex formation, but also play a role in determining the inhibitory activity of the compounds.
SET7/9 inhibitors with an n-hexane chain attached to the N-atom of the azaalkane moiety are more effective than those with an alkyl chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SET7/9 has a unique substrate-binding site and that the alkyl chain is important for binding to the substrate-binding sites and for the recognition of a substrate peptide.
the N atom in the alkyl chain in the inhibitor is crucial for the inhibition of SET7/ 9, and the inhibitor binds to the SET7/9 active site in a manner similar to that for the substrate.
azaalkyl groups of the AdoMet analogs are important for the inhibition mechanism of SET7/ 9.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the alkyl chain in the inhibitors of SET7 binds in the lysate-access channel of SET7/ and the alkyl chain length and interactions of the inhibitors with the substrate-binding site and the lysine-access channels are important determinants of the inhibitory activity of the inhibitors of SET.
SET7/9 can accommodate inhibitors with a wide range of structures and sizes.
the lysine-access channels of SET7/7 and SET8, which have a similar overall structure, are not only involved in substrate recognition but also in inhibitor recognition.
